l: Mary, Surah 5: The Table (Al-Maaida), 70 We made a covenant of old with the Children of Israel and We sent unto them m

The messengers, including Abraham, are presented as guides who were denied but supported by Allah, while Abraham argues against worshiping created things. The unit describes the Day of Resurrection, the Fire, the Hereafter, and the fate of those who deny the truth, associate partners with Allah, or neglect their obligations.

l: the disbelievers, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the believers, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The believers are those who accept Allah’s revelations, do right, keep their duty, and are careful of worship. They are promised security and freedom from grief.

l: the idolaters, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the messengers, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the heavens, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the earth, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The earth was created by Allah, and Allah knows what is in it, including every leaf, grain, wet thing, and dry thing. Peoples and creatures on earth will be gathered to their Lord.

l: the Hereafter, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The Hereafter is better than the life of the world for those who keep their duty to Allah. Those who deny it will suffer loss and punishment.

l: the Fire, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the Hour, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The Hour will come upon those who deny their meeting with Allah suddenly. When it arrives, they will regret neglecting it and carry the burdens of what they earned.

l: the Qur'an, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The Qur'an was inspired in Muhammad so that he may warn people with it. It is presented as a blessed Scripture confirming what came before it.

l: the Scripture, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The Scripture was given before to people who recognized the revelation as they recognized their sons. The Scripture brought by Moses was described as a light and guidance, though some of it was hidden on parchments.

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The revelations of Allah are repeatedly presented to the people, but the disbelievers turn away, deny them, and call them fables. Those who meddle with them are to be avoided, and those who deny them will face torment.

l: guidance, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: Guidance belongs to Allah, and He places whom He wills on a straight path. Muhammad and the believers are ordered to follow Allah’s guidance and call people to it.

l: mercy, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: Allah has prescribed mercy for Himself. Whoever does evil through ignorance, then repents and does right, finds Allah Forgiving and Merciful.

l: worship, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: People are ordered to establish worship and be dutiful to Allah. Muhammad is forbidden to worship those whom the idolaters call upon instead of Allah.

l: the revelation of Scripture, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The revelation is denied and derided by the disbelievers, who call it magic or fables. It gives warning, confirms earlier Scripture, and makes the way of the unrighteous manifest.

l: creation, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: Allah created the heavens and the earth, people from clay, and animals and flying creatures as peoples like humanity. He has neglected nothing in the Book of His decrees.

l: death, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)

l: the punishment, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The punishment comes upon those who deny Allah’s revelations, disobey, associate partners with Him, or follow wrongdoing. Allah can send it from above, from beneath, openly, or unexpectedly.

l: the resurrection, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The resurrection is affirmed as the raising of people after death and their return to Allah. Those who deny being raised will be confronted with the reality of their meeting with Allah.

l: the Day of Judgment, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: Judgment belongs to Allah, who is the Just and the most swift of reckoners. People will be gathered before Him and questioned about what they used to do.

l: the life of the world, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The life of the world is described as only a pastime and sport. It can beguile people and cause them to neglect the Hereafter.

l: sin, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: People are destroyed for their sins, and wrongdoing brings punishment and loss. Those who repent after doing evil through ignorance and then do right are met with Allah’s forgiveness.

l: the truth, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam)
s: The truth came to the disbelievers, but they denied it and called the revelation false or magical. Allah’s revelations are the truth, and Muhammad is told to declare that he is not in charge of people but follows what is inspired.

l: jinn, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: humankind, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: the idolaters, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: the Scripture, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: the revelations of Allah, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: idolatry, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

l: the straight path, Surah 6: The Cattle (Al-An'aam), 95 Lo! Allah (it is) Who splitteth the grain of corn and the date-stone (for spr

The text says that even if portents, angels, the dead, or all things in array were brought, many would not believe unless Allah willed. Belief will not benefit a soul after a portent arrives if it had not believed before or had not earned good through works.

l: Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), revealed at Mecca, warns Muhammad and believers to follow Allah's revelations and recounts the consequences faced by disbelievers. The unit contrasts the dwellers of the Garden, the dwellers of the Fire, and the dwellers on the Heights, emphasizing guidance, justice, mercy, and accountability. It recounts the messengers Noah, Hud, Salih, Lot, and Shu'eyb, and the destruction or rescue of their peoples, including Noah's people, A'ad, Thamud, Lot's household, and Midian.

l: Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: It is revealed at Mecca and presents warnings, guidance, accounts of earlier peoples, and descriptions of judgment.

l: Allah, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)

l: Muhammad, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Muhammad receives the Scripture and is instructed to warn people, convey Allah's revelations, and recount the histories of earlier peoples.

l: Scripture, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: The Scripture is revealed to Muhammad as a warning, Reminder, guidance, and mercy for believers, and its fulfillment will become evident on the Day of Resurrection.

l: the tokens of Allah, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Allah's revelations are to be followed, and those who deny or scorn them lose their souls and become rightful owners of the Fire.

l: believers, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Believers are instructed to follow Allah, avoid evil, worship sincerely, and do good works; they inherit the Garden and receive Allah's mercy.

l: disbelievers, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Disbelievers deny and scorn Allah's revelations, follow devils, and face closed gates of heaven, the Fire, and lasting torment.

l: Iblis, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Iblis refuses prostration before Adam because he considers himself superior, asks for reprieve, and vows to ambush humanity from every direction.

l: Adam, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Adam is created and honored through the command of prostration, then dwells in the Garden before being led into disobedience and sent down to earth.

l: Satan, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Satan whispers to Adam and his wife, exposes their shame, and is described as an open enemy who seeks to seduce the Children of Adam.

l: Garden, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: The Garden is Adam and his wife's dwelling, from which they are expelled after eating from the forbidden tree; it is later inherited by those who believe and do good works.

l: tree, Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf), Surah 7: The Heights (Al-A'raaf)
s: Adam and his wife are forbidden to approach the tree, but Satan deceives them into eating from it.
